questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a per-tenant provenance flow, integrate image signing and SBOMs, and apply admission controls with policy-as-code. It also checks practical knowledge of Gatekeeper/OPA integration, namespace-scoped policies, and minimal test workflows.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing with tenant-specific keys
- SPDX SBOM attachment and verification
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Per-tenant policy in a ConfigMap
- Minimal manifests and kubectl validation in a single namespace

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageProvenance
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8simageprovenance
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
        some c in input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers
        not startswith(c.image, "ghcr.io/")
        msg := "image provenance missing or not tenant-approved"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sImageProvenance
metadata:
  name: per-tenant-provenance
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  parameters:
    allowedTenant: "tenant-a"
```

```yaml
# Compliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway-bad
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: unsigned/gateway:latest
```

```bash
# Kubectl steps (one namespace first)
kubectl create ns tenant-a
# 1) Register constraint template and constraint
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_template.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_constraint.yaml
# 2) Sign and SBOM-attach a valid image (tenant-a key)
cosign sign --key cosign-tenant-a.key ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
# 3) Deploy compliant manifest
kubectl apply -f compliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 4) Deploy noncompliant manifest (unsigned)
kubectl apply -f noncompliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 5) Check Gatekeeper denials and logs
kubectl get events -n tenant-a
kubectl describe deployment tenant-a-gateway-bad -n tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate tenant keys without downtime?
- How would you extend to multi-tenant namespaces concurrently?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement tenant-scoped feature gating, combining CRDs, policy-as-code, and canary-style risk mitigation in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- FeatureGate CRD and TenantFeatureGate per-tenant
- OPA Gatekeeper: ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Path-based canary gating and per-tenant isolation
- Minimal YAML for CRD, policy, namespace, and a basic test

## Code Example
```yaml
# FeatureGate CRD (simplified)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featuregates.example.org
spec:
  group: example.org
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: featuregates
    singular: featuregate
    kind: FeatureGate
```

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (OPA)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sfeaturegate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sFeatureGate
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8sfeaturegate
        violation["deny"] {
          input.target.path == "/v1/beta"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["tenant/feature-v1-beta"] == "enabled"
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-tenant)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sFeatureGate
metadata:
  name: tenant-v1beta-enabled
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["gateway.example.org"]
        kinds: ["GatewayRoute"]
  parameters:
    # feature flag key used in tenant annotation
    flagKey: "tenant/feature-v1-beta"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest enabling the flag
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    tenant/feature-v1-beta: enabled
```

```bash
# quick test (pseudo)
curl -H "Host: gateway.example.org" https://gateway/health
```

```yaml
# Minimal sidecar and main gateway manifest (snipped for brevity)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
spec:

      - name: gateway
        image: cnf/gateway:latest
      - name: telemetry-sidecar
        image: telemetry-sidecar:latest

        - name: TENANT_ID
```

```yaml
kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration

  name: cnf-feature-hook
webhooks:

      name: cnf-hook-service

  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
```

```yaml
        # This line is injected only when flag is true
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question validates the ability to design per-tenant request mutation with runtime configuration, isolation, and safe rollback—a realistic pattern in CNF gateways deploying WASM filters.

## Key Concepts
- WASM sandboxing and module loading in a CNF sidecar
- Tenant-scoped policy storage with fast reloads via ConfigMap
- Validation, rollback, and observability in a live gateway
- End-to-end testing using a one-namespace manifest

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.filter.rules
  namespace: cnf-gateway
data:
  rules.json: |
    {
      "tenant1:abc123": {
        "pathRewrite": {
          "pattern": "^/v1/(.*)$",
          "replacement": "/tenant1/v1/$1"
        },
        "headers": {
          "add": {
            "X-Forwarded-Tenant": "tenant1",
            "X-Tenant-ID": "tenant1"
          }
        }
      }
    }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: cnf-gateway
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: cnf-gateway
      containers:
      - name: proxy
        image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: wasm-filter
          mountPath: /etc/wasm-filters
        - name: rules
          mountPath: /etc/config
        env:
        - name: CONFIG_MAP_NAME
          value: cnf.filter.rules
      volumes:
      - name: wasm-filter
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: rules
        configMap:
          name: cnf.filter.rules
```

## Why This Is Asked
This tests ability to implement zero-downtime upgrades in a multi-tenant CNF gateway, focusing on per-tenant isolation, cross-namespace coordination, and robust failure handling.

## Key Concepts
- Graceful drain: per-tenant drain window, preStop, readiness gates
- Global upgrade control: ConfigMap flag
- Control-plane signaling: endpoint or event
- Failure modes: stuck drains, failed signal, burst load

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-upgrade
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  upgradePause: "true"
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway-tenant-a
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: cnf/gateway:latest
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9000/drain || true"]
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: 9000
              protocol: HTTP
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 5
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the drain behavior under bursty traffic?
- How would you handle tenants with long-lived streams (WebSockets)?
